## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r Graphing Template}
# Graphing template
ggplot(data = <DATA>) + <GEOM_FUNCTION>(mapping = eas(<MAPPINGS>))

# Graphing Aesthetics
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class))
```

```{r size class graph}
# Change point size by class
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, size = class))
```

```{r transparency graph}
# Change point transparency by class (alpha)
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, alpha = class))
```

```{r Graph point shape by class}
# Changing plot points on the graph to be shapes according to class
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, shape = class))
```

```{r Manual Graph Aesthetic}
# Set properties manually, such as offering a number or a colour
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), color = "blue")

# other manual appearance alterations include the name of a color as a character string, the size of a point in mm, the shape of a point as a number
```

```{r}
# testing out mapping an aesthetic to something other than a variable name
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), color = displ < 5)
# says object 'displ' not found
```

```{r Facet and Panel plots}
# Use facet_wrap() function to split up data into sub plots  using a single variable - only use discrete variables
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  facet_wrap(~ class)
```

```{r 2 varaible facet}
# to split up graphs using more than one variable, split them using ~
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  facet_grid(drv ~ cyl)
```

```{r}
# use a . if you do not want to facet in the rows or column dimension
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  facet_grid(. ~ cyl)
```

```{r Fitting simple lines}
# To display data as points, use geom_point()
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))

# To display same data as a smooth line fit through the points, use geom_smooth()
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))

# geom is what represents the data, change the geom function to change geom type (or how the data is represented)

# can change line type using a variable to control it
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, linetype = drv))
# separates the cars into three different line types based on drv (front wheel, rear wheel, or 4wd)

# Use group argument to show that our data is in fact grouped
ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, group = drv))

# Change the color of each line based on drv value
ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = drv),
    show.legend = FALSE)

# Plot multiple geoms on the single plot - add commands together
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))

# To specify different data for each layer use the "subcompact" to select a subset of the data and plot only that subset
install.packages("ggplot2")
install.packages("dplyr")
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(color = class)) + 
  geom_smooth(data = dplyr::filter(mpg, class == "subcompact"),se = FALSE)

```

```{r Transformations and Stats}
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut))
# Alternative method:
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  stat_count(mapping = aes(x = cut))

# to override default settings:
demo <- tribble(
  ~cut,         ~freq,
  "Fair",       1610,
  "Good",       4906,
  "Very Good",  12082,
  "Premium",    13791,
  "Ideal",      21551
)
demo

ggplot(data = demo) +
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = freq), stat = "identity")
# this allows the data to be categorized by cut and the frequency to be plotted on the y axis, instead of counting the number of occurrences of each cut and plotting that on the y axis.

# Display proportion of total dimond dataset rather than count, overriding a default mapping from transformed variables to aesthetics
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = stat(prop), group = 1))
# Warning is ok

# Plotting statistical details, show more about transformations in your plot
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  stat_summary(
    mapping = aes(x = cut, y = depth),
    fun.min = min,
    fun.max = max,
    fun = median
  )
```

```{r Aesthetic Adjustments}
# Aesthetic adjustments
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, colour = cut))
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = cut))

# Use position arugment with clarity
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity))

# Position adjustment allows customising plots in 3 ways: identiy (raw data), fill (changes heights), dodge (forces ggplot2 to not put things on top of each other)

# Identity places each object exactly where it falls in the context of the graph
#To alter transparency (alpha)
ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity)) + 
  geom_bar(alpha = 1/5, position = "identity")

#To color the bar outlines with no fill color
ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes(x = cut, colour = clarity)) + 
  geom_bar(fill = NA, position = "identity")

# Fill works like stacking but makes each set of stacked bars the same height
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity), position = "fill")

# Dodge places overlapping objects side by side
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity), position = "dodge")

# Jitter adds a small amount of random noise to each point to avoid over-plotting when points overlap
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), position = "jitter")
```

```{r Layered grammer of graphics}
# Template for making ggplot2 with position adjustments, stats, and faceting
ggplot(data = <DATA>) + 
  <GEOM_FUNCTION>(
     mapping = aes(<MAPPINGS>),
     stat = <STAT>, 
     position = <POSITION>
  ) +
  <FACET_FUNCTION>
```

```{r Filtering your data}
# Simple Example: Checking Sea Surface Temperature (SST)
sst <- 30.2

if (sst > 29.5) {
  print("Warning: Marine heatwave threshold exceeded!")
} else {
  print("SST remains within baseline parameters.")
}
# Prints: "Warning: Marine heatwave threshold exceeded!"


# Tidyverse Alternative: Vectorised Conditions (dplyr)
# if_else()
library(tidyverse)
# Sample coral data
coral_monitoring <- tibble(
  site = c("Site_A", "Site_B", "Site_C"),
  depth_m = c(12, 35, 8)
)
# Classify depth using if_else
coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>% 
  mutate(zone = if_else(depth_m > 30, "Deep Reef", "Shallow Reef"))

## Task ##
# The function mutate() is used to create a new variable called 'zone' based on the condition specified in if_else(). If depth_m is greater than 30, 'zone' will be classified as "Deep Reef"; otherwise, it will be classified as "Shallow Reef". The resulting tibble will show the site, depth, and corresponding zone classification for each monitoring site. - information from AI copilot - %>% is the pipe operator, it takes the output of one function and feeds it into the next function, allowing for a more readable and efficient workflow when performing multiple operations on a dataset. - information from AI copilot - 

# case_when()
# provides clean, sequential evaluation layout using formula tildes
coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>% 
  mutate(reef_category = case_when(
    depth_m < 10  ~ "Lagoon / Flats",
    depth_m <= 30 ~ "Crest / Slope",
    depth_m > 30  ~ "Mesophotic / Deep",
    TRUE          ~ "Unclassified" # Catch-all remainder
  ))
```

```{r Task: Enviro Stress Classification}
# Using the coral_monitoring data, initialize a tibble named marine_stations containing a column for salinity with values 35, 28, 32, and 12. Use the pipe operator(%>%) and mutate() combined with case_when() to create a new column named environment_type. Classify values below 15 as "Estuarine", values between 15 and 30 as "Brackish", and values above 30 as "Marine".
# put into chattr 
library(dplyr)

marine_stations <- tibble(
  salinity = c(35, 28, 32, 12)
) %>%
  mutate(
    environment_type = case_when(
      salinity < 15 ~ "Estuarine",
      salinity >= 15 & salinity <= 30 ~ "Brackish",
      salinity > 30 ~ "Marine",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_ # Default case for any unhandled values
    )
  )

marine_stations
```
